And the fountains of the abyss

et prohibitæ sunt pluviæ de cælo.
And the rain from heaven was restrained.
Reversæque sunt aquæ de terra euntes et redeuntes:
And the waters were restored to their coming and going from the earth.
et cœperunt minui post centum quinquaginta dies.
And they began to diminish after one hundred and fifty days.
And the ark rested in the seventh month,
on the twenty-seventh day of the month,
et decrescebant usque ad decimum mensem:
the waters were departing and decreasing until the tenth month.
on the first day of the month,
the tips of the mountains appeared.
And when forty days had passed,
opening the window that he had made in the ark,
until the waters were dried up across the earth.
Likewise, he sent forth a dove after him,
ut videret si jam cessassent aquæ super faciem terræ.
in order to see if the waters had now ceased upon the face of the earth.
Quæ cum non invenisset ubi requiesceret pes ejus,
But when she did not find a place where her foot might rest,
reversa est ad eum in arcam:
she returned to him in the ark.
aquæ enim erant super universam terram:
For the waters were upon the whole earth.
And he extended his hand and caught her,
and he brought her into the ark.
Expectatis autem ultra septem diebus aliis,
And then, having waited a further seven days,
he again sent forth the dove out of the ark.
At illa venit ad eum ad vesperam,
And she came to him in the evening,
portans ramum olivæ virentibus foliis in ore suo:
carrying in her mouth an olive branch with green leaves.
intellexit ergo Noë quod cessassent aquæ super terram.
Noah then understood that the waters had ceased upon the earth.
And nevertheless, he waited another seven days.
And he sent forth the dove,
quæ non est reversa ultra ad eum.
which no longer returned to him.
Therefore, in the six hundred and first year,
on the first day of the month,
the waters were diminished upon the earth.
And Noah, opening the cover of the ark,
aspexit, viditque quod exsiccata esset superficies terræ.
gazed out and saw that the surface of the earth had become dry.
on the twenty-seventh day of the month,
et vigesimo die mensis arefacta est terra.
Locutus est autem Deus ad Noë,
filii tui et uxores filiorum tuorum tecum.
your sons and the wives of your sons with you.
Bring out with you all the living things that are with you,
tam in volatilibus quam in bestiis et universis reptilibus,
so also with the wild beasts
and all the animals that move upon the earth.
et uxores filiorum ejus cum eo.
and the wives of his sons with him.
et reptilia quæ reptant super terram,
and the animals that move upon the earth,
Then Noah built an altar to the Lord.
taking from each of the cattle and birds that were clean,
he offered holocausts upon the altar.
And the Lord smelled the sweet odor and said:
“I will no longer curse the earth because of man.
Nequaquam ultra maledicam terræ propter homines:
For the feelings and thoughts of the heart of man are prone to evil from his youth.
sensus enim et cogitatio humani cordis in malum prona sunt ab adolescentia sua:
non igitur ultra percutiam omnem animam viventem sicut feci.
I will no longer pierce every living soul as I have done.
All the days of the earth,
night and day, will not cease.”
